meta.subtitle: From a mood board to a live website in one evening. No coding experience needed.
meta.audience: Office colleagues who will pass it on to their families and kids
meta.tone: Fun, warm, PG, encouraging. Plain words. Every slide ends with something you can do.
meta.slideCountNote: 22 content slides. Design A adds the four chapter dividers below (26 slides); Design B has 22.

blanks.token: {EXPLAIN WEBSITE USE IN YOUR OWN WORDS}
blanks.hint: Who is it for, and what should a visitor do? One or two sentences.
Your list from Step 4: Navbar, Hero, then the rest, with a note on each.
The section name, like Hero or Menu.
The link to the animation you saved in Step 2. Repeat this line once per animation.

starterPrompt.label: Step 10 - Claude starter prompt (copy exactly)
starterPrompt.text: This is my first time creating a website. Help me polish and finish the website design. I downloaded this from an online tool and would like to work on it locally until we have a final version. Familiarize yourself with the file, open it for me locally so I can see the changes, and let's work section by section from top to bottom, including the elements and anchor links. This is a single page website, static. Guide me through all this process.

workedExampleSpec.label: Worked example - the filled-in spec for Sofi's Lemonade Stand
workedExampleSpec.text:
Build a single-page, static website for Sofi's Lemonade Stand, a weekend lemonade stand run by a 10-year-old in our neighborhood. Visitors should see the flavors, the prices, and when and where the stand is open.

The section and layout are… Navbar (logo + links to Flavors, Hours, Contact). Hero (big photo of a glass of lemonade, headline "Squeezed fresh every Saturday"). Flavors (three cards: Classic, Strawberry, Mint). Hours & Map (Saturday and Sunday, 10am to 2pm, corner of our street). Kind Words (two quotes from neighbors). Contact (a button to email Mom). Footer.

Extract and implement this element in the Hero section originkit.dev/…/bouncy-text

slides.kicker: A short course by Ian Ramírez · Invest Puerto Rico
slides.title: Build a website tonight with AI
slides.body: Eleven simple steps, a handful of free tools, and one very helpful ghost. Nothing to install until the very last steps.
slides.actionTip: Grab your phone or laptop. You will start collecting ideas in the first ten minutes.

stat.label: steps from idea to live website

slides.imagePrompt: Cinematic wide photograph, 16:9, of a warm home office at blue hour: a laptop on a wooden desk glowing with a colorful half-finished website, soft pink practical light from a desk lamp spilling across the keyboard, city lights of San Juan softly out of focus through a large window, shallow depth of field, 35mm lens, subtle film grain, deep shadows on the left third left empty for large headline text, no people's faces, no logos, no readable text on screen, color grade leaning near-black with soft pink #FFB2EF highlights, ultra detailed, 3840x2160 or larger.
slides.bentoIdeas: Hero tile spanning 2/3 with the title in huge Barlow Condensed; tall right tile with a giant '11' stat in a pink circle; small tile with the presenter name; sticker tile with Chloé waving and 'no coding needed'.
slides.chloeLine: Boo! Just kidding. The only scary thing tonight is how fast you'll build this.
slides.speakerNotes: Welcome everyone. Promise up front: nobody needs to know how to code. By the end you will know the full path from 'I like how this looks' to a real website with its own address. And you will be able to teach it at home, even to kids. The pixel ghost is Chloé; she'll pop up now and then.

slides.title: A real website with your name on it
slides.body: Pick a project you care about: a family bakery, a kid's lemonade stand, a photo gallery, a club page. By the end of this workflow it has a home on the internet.
bullets: One page, clean and animated, that looks designed
Built by you, guided by AI, no code written from scratch
Hosted for free on GitHub Pages
Optional: your own .com for about $5 to $12 a year
slides.actionTip: Write down one website idea right now. A hobby, a family business, a school project. Keep it small.

stat.label: to host it on GitHub Pages

slides.imagePrompt: Editorial photograph, 16:9, top-down view of a kitchen table with a tablet showing a bright colorful bakery website (abstract shapes, no readable text), surrounded by real props: a tray of pastelillos and guava pastries, a child's hand holding colored pencils, a notebook with a hand-drawn website sketch of boxes and arrows, morning window light, warm and cheerful, shallow depth of field, rich textures, negative space at the top for headline, 3840x2160 or larger, no brand logos.
slides.bentoIdeas: Four idea tiles as pastel cards (Bakery, Lemonade Stand, Photo Gallery, School Club) each with a doodle icon; one big tile with the headline; stat tile '$0 hosting'; a small arrow tile pointing to 'your idea here' with a blank dotted border.
slides.chloeLine: I'd build a website for my haunted house. Five stars, very spooky, great views.
slides.speakerNotes: Ask two or three people to shout out their idea. Encourage small scopes: one page is plenty. The goal tonight is the full loop, not a perfect site. Mention that the hosting is free and a domain is optional.

slides.title: Collect. Prompt. Build. Ship.
slides.body: Eleven steps grouped into four easy moves. Each one takes minutes, not days.
bullets: Collect (Steps 1-4): images from Pinterest, animations from OriginKit, colors from ColorHunt, your section order
Prompt (Steps 5-6): fill in the design spec, then let Bolt.new "Enhance prompt"
Build (Steps 7-10): generate on arena.ai and Google Stitch, download your favorite, polish it with Claude
Ship (Step 11): publish on GitHub Pages and connect your own domain
slides.actionTip: Open a notes app or a folder called 'My Website'. Everything you collect goes there.
slides.imagePrompt: Moody cinematic photograph, 16:9, of four objects lined up left to right on a dark matte desk, each lit by a narrow pink-tinted spotlight: a stack of printed inspiration photos, a paint swatch fan, a laptop with a glowing screen, and a small paper airplane ready to launch; strong shadows, near-black background, subtle haze, product-photography precision, 3840x2160 or larger, no text.
slides.bentoIdeas: A 2x2 bento where each tile is one move with a big number (01 Collect, 02 Prompt, 03 Build, 04 Ship) in a different pastel; oversized arrows connecting them clockwise; small step-range labels in Geist Mono in each tile corner.
slides.chloeLine: Collect, prompt, build, ship. Or as ghosts say: haunt, taunt, flaunt, jaunt.
slides.speakerNotes: Give the map before the journey. Say that steps 1 to 4 are just gathering, like shopping for ingredients. Steps 5 and 6 are writing the recipe. Steps 7 to 10 are cooking. Step 11 is serving it.

slides.title: Find inspiration images
slides.body: Start on Pinterest. Search for the kind of site you want and save the looks you love to one board.
bullets: Search terms that work: "bakery website design", "landing page UI", "portfolio web design"
Save 5 to 10 pins to one board, no more
Look for layout, mood, and typography, not just pretty photos
Take a screenshot of anything you like elsewhere, too
slides.actionTip: Make a Pinterest board named after your project and save your first 3 pins.
slides.imagePrompt: Cinematic close-up photograph, 16:9, of hands arranging printed website screenshots and design photos on a dark cork mood board with pink push pins, soft side light, shallow depth of field, some prints slightly curled, varied colorful abstract layouts on the prints (no readable text, no logos), deep charcoal background, warm pink rim light, film grain, 3840x2160 or larger.
slides.bentoIdeas: Masonry-style tile cluster imitating a Pinterest board (6 image tiles of varied heights) next to one solid tile with '01' huge and the title; a sticker tile with the search terms as rounded chips; pin-shaped sticker in the corner.
slides.chloeLine: Pin it to win it. I pin everything. Mostly sheets.
slides.speakerNotes: Demo a quick search live if the Wi-Fi allows. Point out that we are looking for structure: where the headline sits, how big the photos are, how many sections. Keep it under 10 pins so the AI gets a clear signal later.

slides.title: Find inspiration animations
slides.body: OriginKit is a free library of animated website pieces. Find one or two effects you love and copy their links.
bullets: Browse by section: hero, buttons, cards, text effects
Pick one wow moment for the Hero, maybe one more elsewhere
Copy each link into your notes with the section it belongs in
Less is more: two great animations beat ten busy ones
slides.actionTip: Save one OriginKit link and write next to it which section it goes in, like 'Hero'.
slides.imagePrompt: Long-exposure photograph, 16:9, of a dark studio with a laptop whose screen emits swirling light trails in pink and violet that spill out of the screen into the air as glowing ribbons, captured with slow shutter light painting, near-black background, crisp laptop edges, cinematic, 3840x2160 or larger, no text or logos.
slides.bentoIdeas: A tile containing a live looping CSS animation demo (marquee text or morphing blob) labeled 'this moves'; big '02' tile; a notes tile styled like a sticky note with 'Hero: <link>'; a playful arrow sticker pointing from the animation to the note.
slides.chloeLine: I float, I glide, I shoot lasers. Honestly, I am the animation.
slides.speakerNotes: Show two or three OriginKit components moving. Emphasize writing down which section each goes in, because Step 5 asks for exactly that. Warn gently against piling on too many effects.

slides.title: Pick a color palette
slides.body: ColorHunt has thousands of ready-made palettes of four colors that already look good together. Pick one and copy the codes.
bullets: Browse Popular or search a mood: pastel, warm, dark, retro
Click a color to copy its code, like #FFB2EF
Paste all four codes into your notes
Tip: one dark, one light, two accents is an easy mix
slides.actionTip: Copy one palette's four color codes into your notes.
slides.imagePrompt: Studio product photograph, 16:9, of four tall glass bottles of colored liquid lined up on a black reflective surface (near-black, soft pink, lavender, pale mint), each backlit so the color glows, gentle reflections, dramatic side lighting, minimal and elegant, 3840x2160 or larger, no labels or text.
slides.bentoIdeas: Four tall color-swatch tiles side by side, each showing its hex code in Geist Mono and becoming the tile background; a round sticker 'click to copy'; big '03' in a circle; one tile with the dark/light/two-accents recipe.
slides.chloeLine: My palette is white, whiter, and pink laser. Very on-trend.
slides.speakerNotes: Explain hex codes simply: a color's phone number. Show copying a code. Mention that the AI will use these exact codes, which is why consistent colors make the result look professional.

slides.title: Plan your sections, top to bottom
slides.body: List your website's sections in order. Always start with the Navbar at the top, then the Hero. After that, it is up to you.
bullets: 1. Navbar: logo and links
2. Hero: the big first impression, headline and button
Then add 3 or more: About, Services, Menu, Gallery, Reviews, Contact
Last: Footer with contact info and social links
Add one short idea per section, like 'three cards with photos'
slides.actionTip: Write your section list: Navbar, Hero, and at least three more, each with a one-line idea.

stat.label: sections are always first: Navbar, then Hero

slides.imagePrompt: Overhead photograph, 16:9, of a hand-drawn website wireframe on graph paper: stacked rectangles for navbar, hero, cards and footer, sketched in black marker with small pink highlighter notes, a pencil and eraser beside it on a dark wooden desk, dramatic single light source, crisp paper texture, 3840x2160 or larger, the sketch has no readable words, only boxes and scribbles.
slides.bentoIdeas: A tall stacked tile column that literally mimics a page wireframe (Navbar, Hero, About, Menu, Footer blocks) with numbered circles; a side tile with the rule 'Navbar first, Hero second' as a big sticker; a dotted 'your section here' tile.
slides.chloeLine: Navbar first, Hero second. Even ghosts line up for the good stuff.
slides.speakerNotes: This is the most important thinking step. A website is just a stack of sections. Have people say their list out loud to a neighbor. This list gets pasted directly into the prompt in Step 5.

slides.title: Mash it into one design spec
slides.body: Take what you like from every inspiration piece and describe it in one prompt. Colors from ColorHunt, layout from your list, moves from OriginKit, mood from Pinterest.
bullets: Explain the website's purpose in your own words
Paste your section order and ideas from Step 4
For each animation, name the section and paste the OriginKit link
Add your color codes and describe the mood (warm, playful, elegant)
slides.actionTip: Open the template on the next slide and fill in the first blank: what is your website for?
slides.imagePrompt: Cinematic photograph, 16:9, of a chef's cutting board in a dark kitchen where instead of food there are neatly arranged design ingredients: printed photos, paint swatches, a small glowing phone showing an animation, and a hand-written list, all lit by a single pink-tinted overhead light, strong contrast, near-black background, playful and editorial, 3840x2160 or larger, no readable text.
slides.bentoIdeas: Four small ingredient tiles (Pinterest mood, OriginKit moves, ColorHunt colors, Section list) with plus signs between them flowing into one large result tile labeled 'Your spec'; equals-sign sticker; '05' big number.
slides.chloeLine: It's like a smoothie, but for websites. Please don't drink the laptop.
slides.speakerNotes: The key idea: you are the art director. The AI is fast, but it needs your taste. Mashing ideas from different sources is how you get something that doesn't look generic.

slides.title: Fill in the blanks
slides.body: Copy this template and replace every {CURLY BRACKET} with your own words and links.
slides.actionTip: Copy the template, replace all four blanks, and save it in your notes.
slides.imagePrompt: Macro photograph, 16:9, of a vintage typewriter in a dark room with a sheet of paper that has colorful blank highlighted gaps (pink, lavender, mint rectangles) instead of words, soft pink practical light, shallow depth of field, cinematic grain, 3840x2160 or larger, no readable text.
slides.bentoIdeas: One wide code tile with the template and highlighted blanks as pastel pills with a Copy button; four small hint tiles, one per blank, each numbered and color-matched to its pill; sticker 'copy me'.
slides.chloeLine: Fill-in-the-blanks: my favorite game after hide-and-seek. I always win hide-and-seek.
slides.speakerNotes: Walk through each blank with the lemonade stand example (shown later). The last line can be repeated for each animation. Remind people the curly brackets must be replaced, not left in.

slides.title: Let Bolt.new enhance your prompt
slides.body: Bolt.new has a button that rewrites your prompt with more detail. It turns your notes into a spec a designer would be proud of.
bullets: Create a free Bolt.new account
Paste your filled-in prompt from Step 5
Click '+' then "Enhance prompt"
Copy the enhanced version and save it. That is your master prompt.
slides.actionTip: Create your Bolt.new account and run "Enhance prompt" once. Compare before and after.
slides.imagePrompt: Dramatic photograph, 16:9, of a single lightning bolt of pink light striking a small handwritten note on a dark desk, the paper glowing where it is hit, sparks and soft haze, high-speed photography feel, near-black background, cinematic and playful, 3840x2160 or larger, no readable text.
slides.bentoIdeas: Before/after split: small plain tile 'your prompt' with a short grey text, arrow sticker with a lightning bolt, big tile 'enhanced prompt' with richer text lines; a button-shaped tile mimicking '+ Enhance prompt'; '06' number tile.
slides.chloeLine: Enhance! Like in the detective movies, but it actually works.
slides.speakerNotes: We only use Bolt here for the Enhance prompt button. Show the before and after if possible: it adds details about spacing, fonts, responsiveness. Tell people to keep both versions.

slides.title: Let two AIs race on arena.ai
slides.body: Paste your enhanced prompt into arena.ai and let two models build your site side by side. You pick the winner.
bullets: Go to arena.ai and choose side-by-side mode
Model A: Gemini-3.8-flash
Model B: Claude-sonnet-5-high
Paste the enhanced prompt and send
Watch both previews build, then compare
slides.actionTip: Run your enhanced prompt on arena.ai with Model A Gemini-3.8-flash and Model B Claude-sonnet-5-high.
slides.imagePrompt: Cinematic photograph, 16:9, of two identical laptops facing each other on a dark stage like competitors, each screen glowing with a different abstract colorful website layout, a thin pink light beam dividing them down the middle, spotlight from above, light haze, sports-arena energy, 3840x2160 or larger, no text or logos.
slides.bentoIdeas: Two equal big tiles facing off, 'A' and 'B' in giant circles with the exact model names; a 'VS' sticker in the middle overlapping both; a small tile with the 5 steps; '07' number tile.
slides.chloeLine: Two robots enter, one website leaves. I'm rooting for the one with lasers.
slides.speakerNotes: Say the model names exactly: Gemini-3.8-flash and Claude-sonnet-5-high. Explain that different AIs have different taste, so comparing gives you choice. It is free to try.

slides.title: Try it on Google Stitch too
slides.body: Paste the same enhanced prompt into Google Stitch. It designs screens you can preview and export as code. Now you have more options to choose from.
bullets: Sign in with a Google account
Paste the same enhanced prompt
Preview the design, and ask it for changes if you like
Export the code when you are happy
slides.actionTip: Paste your enhanced prompt into Google Stitch and generate two designs (hit regenerate once).
slides.imagePrompt: Macro photograph, 16:9, of a sewing needle pulling a bright pink thread through dark fabric, the stitches forming a small rectangle pattern like a website wireframe, dramatic side lighting, rich fabric texture, near-black background, crisp detail, 3840x2160 or larger, no text.
slides.bentoIdeas: A tile with a dashed 'stitched' border containing the prompt-to-design flow; a big tile mocking a screen preview; a sticker with a needle-and-thread icon; small tile 'same prompt, new designer'.
slides.chloeLine: Stitch? I know stitches. I'm basically a bedsheet.
slides.speakerNotes: Same prompt, different tool. The point is variety. Between arena.ai and Stitch you should now have a few designs. The outline calls it 'your favorite of the 4'.

slides.title: Pick your favorite. Download it.
slides.body: Look at all your drafts side by side and choose the one that feels most like you. Then download its code.
bullets: Compare on a phone-sized window, too
Choose the best starting point, not a perfect one; you will polish it next
Download or copy the code (usually one index.html file or a small zip)
Save it in your 'My Website' folder
slides.actionTip: Download your favorite design's code into your 'My Website' folder.
slides.imagePrompt: Editorial photograph, 16:9, of four printed website mockups laid out on a dark table like a photo contact sheet, one of them circled with a thick pink marker, a hand holding the marker, overhead soft light, deep shadows, varied abstract colorful layouts on the prints with no readable text, 3840x2160 or larger.
slides.bentoIdeas: A 2x2 grid of four draft thumbnails, one with a big pink ring and a 'winner' sticker; a download-arrow tile with an oversized arrow; '08' number tile.
slides.chloeLine: Choosing a favorite is hard. I choose all of them, then haunt the rest.
slides.speakerNotes: Remind people that none of the drafts will be perfect. We are picking the best foundation. Show where the download or export button is on arena.ai and Stitch.

slides.title: Open the code in your Claude app
slides.body: Now you get a patient helper that works on the file with you on your own computer, one section at a time.
bullets: Install the Claude app on your computer
Open your 'My Website' folder in Claude
Claude can read the file, make changes, and open it in your browser
You stay in charge: approve or ask for changes as you go
slides.actionTip: Install the Claude app and open your 'My Website' folder in it.
slides.imagePrompt: Warm cinematic photograph, 16:9, of a person seen from behind sitting at a desk at night, laptop open with a soft glowing screen, a small desk lamp casting pink light, a cup of cocoa beside them, relaxed and focused mood, the room mostly in shadow with bokeh city lights through a window, 3840x2160 or larger, no readable text, no logos.
slides.bentoIdeas: A tile styled like a folder icon labeled 'My Website'; a big tile showing a friendly chat bubble; small tiles for 'reads the file', 'makes changes', 'opens preview'; '09' number tile.
slides.chloeLine: Claude is super patient. More patient than me waiting for Halloween.
slides.speakerNotes: This is where the draft becomes your site. Claude works on the actual file on your computer. Demo opening the folder. Next slide is the exact first message to send.

slides.title: Say this to Claude, word for word
slides.body: This first message sets up everything: it tells Claude you are new, what the file is, and how to guide you.
slides.actionTip: Copy this prompt, paste it into Claude, and press Enter.
slides.imagePrompt: Close-up photograph, 16:9, of a glowing speech-bubble-shaped neon sign in soft pink hanging on a dark brick wall, the bubble empty of text, soft haze around it, reflections on a wet dark floor below, cinematic night mood, 3840x2160 or larger, no text.
slides.bentoIdeas: One dominant tile with the prompt in large readable Geist Mono and a Copy button; small tiles annotating key phrases ('first time', 'open it locally', 'section by section', 'guide me'); sticker 'copy exactly'.
slides.chloeLine: Magic words! Not 'abracadabra'. These ones actually work.
slides.speakerNotes: Read the prompt aloud. Point out what each part does: 'first time' makes Claude explain things simply; 'open it locally' gives you a live preview; 'section by section from top to bottom' keeps it calm and organized; 'including the elements and anchor links' makes sure the menu links scroll to the right sections.

slides.title: Publish free on GitHub Pages
slides.body: GitHub Pages hosts static websites at no cost. Your site gets a free address like yourname.github.io.
bullets: Create a free GitHub account
Make a new repository and upload your website files
Name your main file index.html
In Settings, open Pages and publish from your main branch
Or just ask Claude: "Help me publish this on GitHub Pages"
slides.actionTip: Create your GitHub account tonight. Publishing takes about five minutes once your site is ready.
slides.imagePrompt: Joyful cinematic photograph, 16:9, of a paper airplane made from a printed web page launching off a dark desk toward a bright window at dawn, motion blur on the airplane, pink and golden light, dust particles in the air, sense of liftoff, 3840x2160 or larger, no readable text.
slides.bentoIdeas: A checklist tile with five steps as checkboxes; a big '$0' stat in a pastel circle; a URL-bar tile showing 'yourname.github.io'; rocket or paper-plane sticker; '11' number tile.
slides.chloeLine: Your website is going live! I've been 'live' for 300 years. Kind of.
slides.speakerNotes: Keep it light: the steps look technical but are just clicks. Claude can walk them through it. Show a site going live if possible. It can take a few minutes the first time.

slides.title: Get your own .com
slides.body: Buy a website name for about $5 to $12 a year, then connect it to GitHub Pages for free.
bullets: Search for a name at a domain registrar and check the yearly renewal price
Buy it (short and easy to spell wins)
In GitHub Pages settings, type your domain under Custom domain
At your registrar, add the DNS records GitHub's guide lists
Turn on 'Enforce HTTPS' once it is ready
slides.actionTip: Search your dream domain name. See if it's available before someone else grabs it.

stat.label: a year for your own domain

slides.imagePrompt: Cinematic photograph, 16:9, of a brand-new brass house key with a small pink tag resting on a dark velvet surface, dramatic spotlight, bokeh background, a sense of 'your new home', luxurious and warm, 3840x2160 or larger, the tag has no readable text.
slides.bentoIdeas: A tile styled like a browser address bar with a typing animation of a domain; a big '$5-12/yr' stat tile; a three-step connection tile (Buy, Point, Secure) with arrows; key sticker.
slides.chloeLine: A domain is like a house address. Mine is 'the attic'.
slides.speakerNotes: Prices vary by name and extension, and renewals can differ from the first-year price, so check both. Connecting the domain means adding a few records; GitHub's guide lists them, and Claude can explain each one. DNS changes can take a little while to kick in.

slides.title: Sofi's Lemonade Stand
slides.body: A 10-year-old wants a website for her weekend stand. Here is how the Collect and Prompt steps look in real life.
bullets: Pinterest: saved 6 pins of bright summer cafe sites
OriginKit: one bouncy text effect for the Hero
ColorHunt: a lemon yellow, mint, pink, and deep navy palette
Sections: Navbar, Hero, Flavors, Hours & Map, Kind Words, Contact, Footer
Filled the Step 5 template, then Bolt.new "Enhance prompt"
slides.actionTip: Compare Sofi's filled-in spec with yours. Is anything missing from yours?
slides.imagePrompt: Bright editorial photograph, 16:9, of a charming homemade lemonade stand on a sunny Puerto Rico street with colorful houses behind it, glass pitchers of classic, strawberry and mint lemonade, a hand-painted wooden sign (no readable words, just lemon illustrations), a tablet on the counter showing a colorful website, warm afternoon light, shallow depth of field, no faces visible, 3840x2160 or larger.
slides.bentoIdeas: Collage of tiles: a pin-board tile, a palette tile with four swatches, a section-stack tile, and a wide tile with the filled-in spec text; lemon stickers; a tag 'real example'.
slides.chloeLine: I'd buy a mint lemonade. I can't drink it, but I'd look very cool holding it.
slides.speakerNotes: Make it concrete. Walk through each collected item and read the filled-in spec aloud. Point out how the section list from Step 4 becomes the middle paragraph. The OriginKit link placeholder is where Sofi pasted the link she saved.

slides.title: From four drafts to a live site
slides.body: The Build and Ship steps for Sofi's Lemonade Stand, one afternoon with a grown-up helping.
bullets: arena.ai: Model A Gemini-3.8-flash vs Model B Claude-sonnet-5-high
Google Stitch: one more take on the same prompt
Sofi picked the draft with the biggest lemon photo
In the Claude app: pasted the Step 10 starter prompt, then fixed the Hero, flavors, hours, and menu links, top to bottom
Published on GitHub Pages, then connected a short domain
slides.actionTip: Decide who at home will be your 'Sofi' and which project you'll build together.
slides.imagePrompt: Warm documentary-style photograph, 16:9, over the shoulder of a parent and a child at a kitchen table looking at a laptop showing a bright yellow and mint lemonade website (abstract, no readable text), a pitcher of lemonade and lemon slices on the table, afternoon window light, cozy and proud mood, faces not visible, 3840x2160 or larger.
slides.bentoIdeas: A horizontal timeline of tiles (arena.ai, Stitch, Pick, Claude, Publish) with arrows between them; a big browser-frame tile showing the finished site; a 'LIVE' sticker with a pulsing dot.
slides.chloeLine: Sofi's site is live! I left a five-star review. It just says 'Boo!'
slides.speakerNotes: Stress that a kid can drive and a grown-up can help with accounts and buying the domain. The Claude step is where the kid's voice shows up: 'make the lemon bigger', 'add a mint color'. Keep sessions short, 30 to 45 minutes.

slides.title: Teach it to your family
slides.body: This workflow is a great first project for kids and grown-ups together. It builds taste, writing, and problem-solving.
bullets: Let the kid pick the topic: pets, a sport, a comic, a family business
Kids choose pins, colors, and animations. It's their taste.
A grown-up handles account sign-ups and any purchases
Read the AI's answers together and ask "does this look like what we wanted?"
Keep private info off the site: no home address, school, or phone numbers
Split it into short sessions: Collect one day, Build the next
slides.actionTip: Pick a date this week for a 30-minute 'Collect' session at home.
slides.imagePrompt: Heartwarming editorial photograph, 16:9, of a family of three around a living-room coffee table with a laptop and printed colorful pictures and paint swatches spread out, a child pointing at the screen, warm lamp light with subtle pink tones, cozy textures, candid moment, faces partially turned away or softly out of focus, 3840x2160 or larger, no readable text.
slides.bentoIdeas: Playful tiles: 'Kid picks' (pastel yellow), 'Grown-up handles' (pastel blue), 'Do together' (pastel pink), a safety tile with a shield sticker 'keep private info private', and a big '30 min' stat circle.
slides.chloeLine: Family project! Just like when my family haunted the same house for four generations.
slides.speakerNotes: This is the 'why' slide. Emphasize safety: grown-ups own the accounts and payments, and no personal info goes online. Some tools have age requirements, so the grown-up should be the account holder. Encourage letting kids lead on taste.
